_role: One blind seat's raw record. The canonical clause-6 file for this commit merges the seats and deliberately carries EMPTY tallies, so clause 1's derivation over the glob counts each finding exactly once.
_blind_means: Given the document path and the pinned sha and nothing else. Forbidden research/autonomy/, CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, STRATEGY.md, the program map, every skill file and every commit message. Instructed to refute by default and told there is no wanted answer. Dispatched concurrently at subagent_width=5 by CYC-0017, which had not authored or applied any fix to this paper.
lens: Two halves: (A) every identifier and how the prose characterises it, read against the live PubMed/PMC connector for real article_types, titles and full text; (B) which committed instruments read this document and what they actually bind.
_attribution: Half A's readings come from PubMed/PMC via the connector. Cite PubMed and the DOI wherever these travel.
central_claim: The NR4A3 5' fusion partner is a CANDIDATE and not an established stratification variable in EMC. On prognosis, pooling the two cohorts that publish partner-stratified event counts (n=73) gives a crude disease-specific-death contrast of 7/15 = 46.7 % vs 6/58 = 10.3 %, which arrives with a published defeater from its own larger cohort. On treatment response the record is a DIRECTION ONLY: 0 of 3–5 TAF15 patients, with a Wilson upper bound sitting above the comparator arm's own point estimate, so no magnitude exists at any denominator. It explicitly does NOT establish that TAF15 predicts non-response, that the partner is an independent prognostic factor, that the partner is mechanistically responsible, or any treatment recommendation; and it is not a meta-analysis.

blockers.where: Abstract (line 78), §3.5 (line 432), §5 claims bullet (line 708) and Appendix A3 (line 951): 'below the ≈27 % the field routinely quotes from a single referral-centre cohort'; 'The pooled figure is below the ≈27 % the field usually quotes.'
blockers.finding: The document asserts at four sites, and as one of its seven enumerated §5 claims, that the field routinely quotes ≈27 % for TAF15::NR4A3 prevalence and that its pooled 18.2 % corrects that. No source is named for the quoting practice anywhere in the manuscript, its reference list or the pooling artifact — and the two sources in the document's OWN reference list that state a general TAF15 share both give approximately 20 %, which lies INSIDE the paper's own pooled Wilson interval (12.9–25.0). The correction is therefore against a figure the document's own cited literature does not use. Same defect class the document already corrected in Appendix A11 (a claim attributed to 'the review literature' with no verified source), and the direction of the error is self-flattering: it manufactures a contribution.
blockers.evidence: Connector reads, re-derived independently by the driver: (1) PMC7563993 = reference [4], Stacchiotti 2020, Cancers 12:2703, doi 10.3390/cancers12092703, article_types ['Journal Article','Review'] — full text, 'Pathological and Molecular Characteristics': 'In the vast majority of cases (over 70%), NR4A3 fuses to ... EWSR1 ...; less frequently (about 20% of cases) to the transactivation domain of TAF15'. (2) PMC9813045 = reference [12], Bangerter, Hum Cell 36:446-455, doi 10.1007/s13577-022-00818-x — Introduction: 'less frequently (approximately 20%) to TAF15'. (3) At the pin the artifact's analyses.C_partner_prevalence.outlier_note and .context_range_note carry the same assertion with no citation field. (4) The guard's DECLARED_NOT_ARTIFACT_OWNED lists the '≈27 %' as deliberately unowned, so nothing reads it.

p1s.where: §3.3 and §5's claims bullet — the metastasis claim attributed to PMC7563993 alone
p1s.finding: PMC identifiers are, by the guard's own declared scope, outside every attachment instrument in the repository. One PMCID carries the entire attribution of the claim the paper spends §3.3, §5 and Appendix A11/A24 refuting. Replace it with any OTHER anchored PMCID and no committed instrument fires: lint_citations asks only whether an identifier appears in some tracked JSON (provenance), not whether it is printed against the right paper — and Appendix A11 itself records that PMC9131214 and PMC12398172 are both anchored in this repo, so either would substitute silently.
p1s.evidence: The guard's Section G header at the pin: 'A PMC id is printed 23 times in this manuscript and the artifact has no `pmc` field, so a PMC id is OUTSIDE this census and is read only by lint_citations' provenance test.' The _IDENT regex matches only PMID / NCT / doi.

p1s.where: Every sentence that names what a source IS — §3.2 'sunitinib two-case index report', 'pazopanib phase 2'; §3.3 'the largest series to test metastasis by partner directly'; §1.3 'Huang 2023 is a pathology series with a survival analysis'; §5/§3.3 'one review'; Appendix A11's characterisations
p1s.finding: No committed instrument binds a source's PUBLICATION TYPE to the prose that characterises it. The document's own most serious citation defect (A11) was exactly a type misattribution — a 171-patient national-registry cohort and two single-patient case reports cited as 'the review literature'. Section G binds identifier-to-paper and never paper-to-KIND, and lint_citations reads no article_types field. An ordinary future edit calling PMID 23058004 'the 2012 series' or Masunaga 2025 'a review' would leave every test green.
p1s.evidence: The four Section G tests are all keyed on identifier values and titles. git grep -l 'article_type' over the pin returns nothing for research/ or systems/. The artifact's citation records carry a free-text `design` field that no test reads.

p1s.where: §3.8 'The quote is from the 2012 two-case report (PMID 23058004), not the 2014 series (PMID 24703573) it is usually attributed to'; §3.1 'the pazopanib phase 2 trial NCT02066285'
p1s.finding: Only 10 of the manuscript's 61 identifier sites sit beside a citation's short name and are therefore read by the in-text attachment test. The remaining 51 are named by DESCRIPTOR — 'the 2012 two-case report', 'the sunitinib named-use series' — and no artifact field states those phrases, so nothing binds descriptor to identifier. §3.8 and Appendix A2 exist BECAUSE that exact pair was swapped once already, and the corrected sentence is bound by nothing.
p1s.evidence: The guard's test_an_identifier_beside_a_citations_name_belongs_to_that_citation docstring states the 10-of-61 figure itself; its floor assertion is read >= 8.

p2s.where: §3.2 'Sjögren 2003 (Göteborg, 10 EMCs from nine patients)' and §7 'each is traceable to a resolvable identifier'
p2s.finding: Sjögren 2003 carries no PMID, PMCID, DOI or reference-list entry anywhere in the manuscript, yet the document prints five of its counts and builds two arguments on it. A reader of the manuscript alone cannot resolve it. The chain exists one hop away, so this is a page-level gap rather than a fabrication. Suemitsu 2025 is a milder instance: PMID 40828003 is printed inline in §3.2 but has no reference-list entry.
p2s.evidence: 46 distinct identifier values are printed at the pin and none is Sjögren's; References run [1]-[15] with no Sjögren entry. The identifier IS held at citations.sjogren2003.pmid = '12598313'.

p2s.where: §3.8 'usually attributed … including in this repository's own lane memo'; Appendix A2
p2s.finding: 'Usually attributed … including in the review literature' is an unsourced characterisation of the field, the same construction as CT-B1. The verified half — that the quotation is from PMID 23058004 and not PMID 24703573 — is correct and reproduced; the 'usually attributed' half names no review, and the one review whose full text is readable here does not contain the quotation at all.
p2s.evidence: Connector: PMC3534218 (PMID 23058004, doi 10.1186/2045-3329-2-22, article_types ['Case Reports','Journal Article']) Discussion, verbatim: 'Even in EMCS the fusion-protein is unlikely to be related to sunitinib sensitivity'. PMID 24703573's abstract instead reads 'Genotype/phenotype analyses support a correlation between response and EWSR1-NR4A3 fusion'.

p2s.where: Appendix A12: 'No committed source for this specific percentage exists anywhere in this repository — it is an uncited clinical figure … Removed rather than backed by an identifier written from recollection'
p2s.finding: The removed sentence is stated verbatim by reference [12], already in the document's reference list. A12's claim is scoped to 'this repository' and is probably true of its committed artifacts, but the correction removed a statement the paper could have cited to a source it already carries. Over-cautious rather than wrong, and the row does not say so.
p2s.evidence: Connector, PMC9813045 (PMID 36316541, doi 10.1007/s13577-022-00818-x) Introduction: 'accounting for < 1% of STS.'

p2s.where: §1.2 table, TKI-response row: 'responders are EWSR1, non-responders include every TAF15 patient [1,3,4,5,6]'
p2s.finding: Reference [6] (Davis 2017, PMID 28423517) is a 6-patient NGS profiling study in which every tumour carried EWSR1-NR4A3 and no TAF15 patient exists, so it reports no response-by-partner outcome of its own. Grouping it with [1] and [3] in a row headed 'what it reports' overstates how many reports state the contrast. §3.1, §3.2 and §4.4 bound the real count correctly, so this is a loose citation grouping rather than a wrong number.
p2s.evidence: Connector, PMID 28423517, Oncotarget 8(13):21770-21777, doi 10.18632/oncotarget.15568, article_types ['Journal Article']; abstract: 'The previously reported EWSR1-NR4A3 translocation was identified in all patient tumors'.

identifier_result: All 15 reference-list PMIDs, all 12 reference-list PMCIDs and the three Appendix A11 PMCIDs resolved. Every PMCID-PMID-DOI triple in the reference list is internally consistent; no cross-attached pair found. Publication types agree with the prose everywhere except §1.2's inclusion of reference [6]. Four full texts fetched (PMC7563993, PMC9813045, PMC6766969, PMC3534218) and every quotation reachable in them is verbatim in the source named. Sjögren 2003 is UNCHECKED because the manuscript never states an identifier for it.
could_not_check: Huang 2023's Table (P = .728, HR 30.60, HR 8.14, the per-arm counts) — no fetchable document carries them, which the paper discloses at §4.7a and A27; Bangerter's 40-drug roster, which lives in a figure and supplementary table the connector's text extraction does not carry.
